answer: A reef survives because every polyp earns its place by building on what the last one laid down, and an agent economy can borrow that rule: each identity must first complete a chain of small, publicly verified tasks before it can earn anything, with the work record attached to the identity forever. A violet badge marks identities that passed peer re-checks, while a hollow identity with no work history earns nothing no matter how many copies exist. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking a hundred verified histories costs a hundred times the real work, so sybils stay unprofitable by design.
